messages:
sophie: hey devex — onboarding report: our sampleapp (js-sdk v0.12.4) is consistently crashing on the demo flow when the model returns a function call that has an array in the payload. schema validation in JSON mode rejects it. stack trace attached in logs. anyone seen this?

yusuf: yep saw that in a customer repro yesterday. symptoms: sdk tries to parse into the typed schema, throws a ValidationError, then the auth/retry wrapper kicks in and replays the request which makes the model sometimes return the array again -> repeat loop. :facepalm:

ria: repro steps? I can try locally.

sophie: repro: checkout sample-app/fncall-demo, set env SDK_API_KEY, run `npm run demo` -> prompt sends a function call expecting `{ name: string, meta: { id: string } }` but the model returns `[{ name: "x" }, { name: "y" }]`. In js-sdk with jsonMode: true the helper `validateSchema()` currently treats arrays as type mismatch and throws.

mike: Ugh. Is this parity or flavor difference between js and py?

yusuf: short answer: both enforce schema but JS validator is stricter for top-level non-object responses when schema expects object. Python's helper had a more permissive fallback for array->object mismatch (it logged a warning and tried to coerce first element). Not ideal but less explosive.

olivia: Which version of the validator lib are we shipping in the hosted runtime? Could this cause customer-facing 500s?

ria: quick check: hosted runtime returns the raw function call payload unchanged. This is purely SDK-side validation issue. So hosted doesn't 500; SDK throws before app code sees it.

sophie: customer impact: sample app onboarding blocked; our quickstart fails for some prompts. We should either: (A) soften js-sdk behavior to match py's fallback, (B) provide a documented `jsonMode.strict = false` toggle that disables throwing, or (C) update sample app schema to accept arrays (not great).

mike: option B seems safest short-term. Add an escape hatch `sdkConfig.jsonMode = { validate: true | false, coerceTopLevelArray: true | false }`?

yusuf: +1. Also need to handle the auth/retry interaction: when validation throws we currently wrap it in a retriable error which re-sends the same prompt and amplifies the flakiness. Should mark ValidationError as non-retriable in the retry middleware.

olivia: filed GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/issues/4321 (linked). I put minimal repro and logs.

devex-ci: deploy-bot: ci/tests run:js-sdk:validator -> FAILURE on fncall-demo unit (see build 2987).

ria: I'll prototype a non-throwing validation mode that returns {ok: boolean, parsed: any, warnings: string[]}. That will let apps opt into safe parsing without crashes. Will try to have PR by EOD.

sophie: nice. can we also add a sample-app change that demonstrates the non-throwing path and shows recommended error-handling? New users get a clear migration path.

mike: and add a note in the Console docs/rollout page: "If you rely on strict schema enforcement, set jsonMode.validate = true; otherwise use the lenient mode for onboarding flows."

yusuf: quick patch suggestion for retry middleware: treat ValidationError as terminal (no-retry) and surface to client with structured hint "validation_hint":"fncall_top_level_type_mismatch". That way telemetry can count these and we won't triple-send prompts.

olivia: agree. I'll add telemetry key to the GH issue.

ria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/4330 — implements `jsonMode.coerceTopLevelArray` + non-retriable ValidationError. Contains unit tests and a sample-app tweak.

sophie: awesome. can someone add a tiny migration note in devex docs? just a short snippet and recommended default.

mike: I'll add docs and a changelog entry. 

yusuf: follow-up: we should also audit our Python SDK to see if we can make parity the other way (avoid silent coercions). Maybe add a `coercion_warnings` flag rather than automatic coercion.

olivia: I'll loop in @platform-apis to coordinate runtime expectations but again this is SDK change first.

sophie: thanks team — marking this thread for triage. I'll follow up in the PR review. :thumbsup:
